title: Emergent activity powers a path to chaos for pairs of acoustically trapped spheres
authors: Matthew K. Gronert, Ben Cao, Ella M. King, David G. Grier
abstract: Pairs of spheres sharing an acoustic trap sometimes spin intermittently despite having no self-propulsion, no obvious power source, and no symmetry-breaking mechanism, switching between rocking and spinning within a single trajectory. Nonreciprocal wave scattering powers this emergent activity, and drag shapes their dynamics by coupling rotations to translations. Mismatched pairs can pass through a supercritical Hopf bifurcation into a quasiperiodic torus on which the pair's orbit reverses regularly and, farther from equilibrium, into deterministic chaos. Experiments motivate this mechanism and share its qualitative signatures; simulations reveal a full noise-free route from passivity to chaos, and suggest how analogous dynamics can emerge in other active-matter systems.
summary: This work models the dynamics of two acoustically trapped spheres, demonstrating that non-reciprocal forces can drive the system from a stable, passive state into complex, deterministic chaos. The transition follows a predictable route through a quasiperiodic torus, providing a fundamental example of how non-equilibrium physics can generate complex dynamics without external noise or self-propulsion.
main_problem: The paper investigates the emergence of autonomous, non-steady activity and the subsequent transition to deterministic chaos in a pair of acoustically trapped spheres.
main_result: The system exhibits a clear, noise-free path from a passive, stable state to a quasiperiodic torus, and finally into deterministic chaos, driven solely by non-reciprocal wave scattering forces.
method: The analysis combines theoretical modeling using coupled equations of motion with experimental validation of the observed dynamic regimes.
model_or_system: The system consists of two solid spheres trapped in a standing acoustic wave, whose dynamics are governed by coupled equations involving trapping potentials, drag forces, and non-reciprocal forces arising from size mismatch.
key_observables: Emergent activity (intermittent spinning/twitching), Lyapunov exponent ($\lambda$), Poincaré sections, and the system's asymptotic state (passive, quasiperiodic, chaotic).
important_parameters: The dimensionless activity number $S(a, b)$, the non-reciprocal force threshold $F_c$, and the dimensionless distance from threshold $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The model relies on linearizing equations of motion about equilibrium and uses approximations for wave-mediated interactions, though the qualitative picture is claimed to be robust to higher-order corrections.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition through Poincaré sections, showing the progression from a stable torus ($\epsilon=0.31$) to weak chaos ($\epsilon=1$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the governing equations, analyzes the stability of the passive state using bifurcation theory, maps out the transition from stable equilibrium to Hopf bifurcation (librations), and finally characterizes the route to chaos via quasiperiodicity.
why_interesting: The mechanism of chaos generation—driven by non-reciprocal forces and dissipation in a classical mechanical system—provides a clean, non-quantum analogue for understanding how complex, non-equilibrium dynamics can emerge in many-body systems.
